'''''Cotoneaster franchetii''''' ('''[[Adrien René Franchet|Franchet]]'s cotoneaster''' or '''orange cotoneaster''') is a species of ''[[Cotoneaster]]'' native to southwestern [[China]], in the provinces of [[Guizhou]], [[Sichuan]], [[Tibet Autonomous Region|Tibet]], and [[Yunnan]], and also in adjacent northern [[Myanmar]] and northern [[Thailand]].<ref name=foc>{{cite web|url= http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=2&taxon_id=200010732|title=''Cotoneaster franchetii''|publisher=Flora of China|volume=9|accessdate= August 21, 2007}}</ref><ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate=August 21, 2007}}</ref>

It is an [[evergreen]] or semi-evergreen [[shrub]] growing to {{convert|3|m}} tall. The leaves are oval-acute, {{convert|2|–|3.5|cm}} long and {{convert|1|–|1.5|cm}} broad, shiny green above, pubescent below with dense whitish to yellowish hairs. The flowers are produced in [[corymb]]s of 5–15 together, each flower {{convert|6|–|7|mm}} diameter, with the five petals pink on the outer side, white on the inner side. The fruit is a red [[pome]] {{convert|6|–|9|mm}} diameter; they are eaten by fruit-eating birds who disperse the seeds in their droppings.<ref name=foc/><ref name=fwne>Flora of NW Europe: [http://wbd.etibioinformatics.nl/bis/flora.php?menuentry=soorten&id=2825 ''Cotoneaster franchetii''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304092703/http://wbd.etibioinformatics.nl/bis/flora.php?menuentry=soorten&id=2825 |date=2016-03-04 }}</ref><ref name=rhs>{{cite book|editor=Huxley, A|year=1992|title=''New RHS Dictionary of Gardening''|publisher=[[Macmillan Publishers|Macmillan]]|isbn=0-333-47494-5}}</ref>

Two [[variety (biology)|varieties]] are accepted by some authors,<ref name=rhs/> but not treated as distinct by the [[Flora of China (series)|''Flora of China'']]:<ref name=foc/>
*''Cotoneaster franchetii'' var. ''franchetii'', described above  
*''Cotoneaster franchetii'' var. ''cinerascens'' Rehd, larger, to {{convert|4|m}} tall, with leaves up to {{convert|4|cm}} long, and up to 30 flowers per corymb

Some authors include a third variety, var. ''sternianus'',<ref name=grin/> although more often, this is treated as a distinct species, ''Cotoneaster sternianus''.<ref name=rhs/><ref name=fwne2>Flora of NW Europe: [http://wbd.etibioinformatics.nl/bis/flora.php?menuentry=soorten&id=2828 ''Cotoneaster sternianus''] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20130729080906/http://wbd.etibioinformatics.nl/bis/flora.php?menuentry=soorten&id=2828 |date=2013-07-29 }}</ref> As ''Cotoneaster sternianus'' it has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref>{{cite web |title=''Cotoneaster sternianus'' |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/plants/4678/cotoneaster-sternianus/details |date=2021 |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=30 May 2021 |quote=Synonyms; ''Cotoneaster franchetii'' var. ''sternianus'' }}</ref>

==Cultivation and uses==
''Cotoneaster franchetii'' is a popular [[ornamental plant]]. It has escaped from cultivation and become locally [[naturalisation (biology)|naturalised]] in parts of the British Isles and the [[Pacific Northwest]] of North America,<ref name=fwne/><ref name=rhs/> as well as Northern California.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cal-ipc.org/plants/profile/cotoneaster-franchetii-profile/ | title=Cotoneaster franchetii Profile | date=20 March 2017 }}</ref>

Scientists at the Royal Horticultural Society (RHS) in the UK carried out a study on the effectiveness of hedges for soaking up [[air pollution]], comparing different types of shrubs including cotoneaster, [[Common hawthorn|hawthorn]], and [[western red cedar]]. They found that bushy, hairy-leafed varieties of cotoneaster, such as this, are “super plants” that can help soak up air pollution. On roads with heavy traffic, the dense, hairy-leaved ''Cotoneaster franchetii'' was at least 20% more effective at soaking up air pollution than other shrubs often planted along roadsides.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Media|first=P. A.|date=2021-02-18|title=Experts identify 'super-plant' that absorbs roadside air pollution|url=http://www.theguardian.com/environment/2021/feb/18/experts-identify-super-plant-that-absorbs-roadside-air-pollution|access-date=2021-02-18|website=the Guardian|language=en}}</ref>
